Action Plan:
1. Arrange same-day in-person GP/clinic review for wheeze and dyspnoea; pulse-oximetry and further respiratory assessment to be performed.
2. Patient to obtain and take an over-the-counter non-sedating antihistamine today if accessible; if unavailable, GP to prescribe.
3. Letter to patient’s GP to summarise this telehealth consultation and request urgent assessment ± consideration of oral steroid therapy if asthma exacerbation confirmed.
4. Discussed potential need for steroid treatment depending on in-clinic findings.
5. Patient advised to take existing reliever inhaler if symptoms worsen before review (patient has inhaler from “a couple of months ago”).
6. Safety-net: if increasing shortness of breath, inability to speak in sentences, chest tightness, or dizziness occurs before scheduled review, attend ED or call emergency services.
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: Wheeze and shortness of breath for 2 days, onset after house cleaning with dust exposure.  
• Symptoms: Gradually worsened; worse at night; occasionally cannot finish sentences. No chest pain. No dizziness.  
• Past medical history: Childhood asthma (intermittent; occasional exercise-induced symptoms), seasonal hay fever.  
• Medications: Salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented); not used for current episode. No regular hay-fever medication.  
• Allergies: None known.  
• Social history: Lives ~10 min drive from GP surgery; no other details provided.

Objective:
(No physical examination performed during telehealth visit; no vitals available.)

Assessment & Plan:

1. Wheeze / Shortness of breath
   - Assessment: Suspected asthma exacerbation vs dust-triggered allergic reaction.
   - Differential: Acute upper airway allergy, viral lower respiratory tract infection.
   - Investigations planned: Pulse oximetry, focused respiratory examination ± peak flow/spirometry at GP clinic.
   - Treatment planned: Trial of OTC antihistamine today; consider salbutamol inhaler use if needed; possible oral steroids after assessment.
   - Relevant referrals: Urgent same-day GP/clinic review; summary letter sent.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected: Detailed medication reconciliation (names/doses), smoking status, vitals, objective lung exam.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.
